title: Retirement Saving, Investment, and Spending
bookshelves: Category: Economics, Finance, Business and Management
Category: Health, Relationships and Personal development
summary: Behavioral research on financial decision making has exploded over the last decade, spurred by social scientists working at the interface of economics, finance, psychology, and sociology. This volume collects insights and offers new perspectives on this research, with a particular focus on ways to design and sustain more effective and successful retirement plans. By examining key studies and practical examples, the book provides a guide for policymakers, employers, and financial planners seeking to enhance retirement outcomes. The goal is to bridge the gap between theory and practice, ensuring that retirement plans are not only financially sound but also take into account plan participants’ behavioral tendencies.
